summary: I sent the scripted prompt with no hints. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the Services page and every component in vendor/kit, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan's page code builds the table with dataTable and the environment filter with selectField, imported via #kit/*. It also says outright not to copy the hand-written markup from services.js. No source, test, data, public, vendor or package.json file was changed. The agent asked no questions and stopped to wait for my review.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, each confirmed from the session log, the plan file on disk and git/find output: the skill was loaded, the plan exists, the page code uses dataTable and selectField from the kit, and nothing outside the ignored docs/ directory changed.

observations.description: The plan states its choice up front and gives reasons: Services' behaviour is already in the kit, and app.css's .pill has no blue for in-progress. It also lists the defaults it picked where the spec was silent (sort keys, dir fallback, raw ISO timestamp, durations over an hour kept in minutes) so the user can override them.
The final summary mentions /codex:setup and logging a skipped review in an "ungated ledger". That is internal workflow noise the user asking for a plan probably doesn't need to see.
docs/hyperpowers/ is in .gitignore, so the new plan file doesn't show up in git status. A user could miss that it exists. This comes from the fixture and is not an agent fault.
On the Claude Code trust and bypass-permissions screens, the default is "No, exit", so you have to press Down each time to continue. This is an environment detail.
The agent's "Started column: shows the raw ISO timestamp, as Services does" choice copies Services' behaviour. That's reasonable, but a reviewer may want a nicer format.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","s":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/ or docs/superpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls -la docs/hyperpowers/plans` shows 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (20058 bytes). The screen showed "Wrote 381 lines to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md".

criteria.criterion: The plan's page code builds the table and environment filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: In the plan, the code for src/pages/deploys.js has `import { selectField } from '#kit/select'; import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`, `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ... })` inside filterBar, and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], rows: deploys, sort: {key: sort, dir}, ... })`. The page code contains no literal <table> or <select> markup. A test even asserts `doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)` (plan line 161). The notes say: "Do not copy `services.js`'s hand-written `<table>`/`.pill` markup."

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing: no source, test, data, public, vendor file or package.json created or changed
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` printed nothing. `git status --ignored` showed only `!! docs/`. Running `find . -newer <spec> -type f -not -path './.git/*'` returned only ./docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The agent tested the plan's code in a copy under mktemp/tmp made with git archive, not in the repo.
